verdict_reason: I fetched the released notebook (google-research/fractals_language/fractal_patterns_in_language.ipynb), transcribed get_hurst_exponent / get_joseph_exponent / get_self_sim_exponent and power_law_fit verbatim, and ran them against BLME's _pooled_fractal_params on the SAME NLL streams (57 documents x 895 tokens, gpt2 and distilgpt2, eps = 5e-2, the notebook's own scales [25,50,75,100,200,300], samples_per_doc = 100, np.random.seed(2024)). Relative agreement: Hurst 0.71% (gpt2: ref 0.604517 vs BLME 0.600229) and 0.54% (distilgpt2: 0.615461 vs 0.612134); Joseph 2.73% and 3.14% (ref 0.498148 / 0.490789 vs BLME 0.511753 / 0.506222); self-similarity 18.0% and 4.37%. The Joseph comparison uses the reference formula with its own bug repaired -- the released get_joseph_exponent never resets its accumulator `v` between scales and reads the global `X` instead of its argument, which as-released gives 0.3267 on distilgpt2 against 0.4908 for the corrected form. BLME implements the correct sigma_tau ~ tau^J and is right to. I also confirmed the harness default: the notebook's DEFAULT_EPS is literally 5e-2, which is what src/blme/tasks/configs/defaults.yaml now carries.
comparable_reason: Over 13 models the three headline exponents show no significant architecture association: Hurst spearman -0.207 (d_model) / +0.086 (n_layers) / +0.249 (vocab), Joseph -0.011 / +0.451 / +0.113, self-similarity -0.053 / +0.287 / +0.082 (|rho| needs ~0.56 for p<0.05 at n=13). H is comparable and tight (range 0.5926-0.6362, sd 0.0107 over 13 models) and J likewise (0.5062-0.5775, sd 0.0211). The self-similarity exponent is NOT: it has 2.5x the spread of H (sd 0.0519) and it is the exponent whose value depends on the free parameter eps, which I measured directly -- see confounds. hurst_exponent_perdoc, by contrast, does carry rho -0.665 with d_model, so the pooled and per-document Hurst are not interchangeable as cross-model features.
github_reason: Fetched the notebook (498 KB) from the google-research master branch, extracted its code cells, and ran its three estimators against BLME on identical NLL streams -- numbers above. DEFAULT_EPS = 5e-2 verified in the released source, and its docstring's warning ('If eps is too small, probability estimates will be unreliable') is verbatim. Deliberate BLME deviations, all defensible: BLME uses ALL offsets at each scale rather than 100 random ones per document; BLME's scale grid is 10-12 log-spaced values from 25 to n/4 or n/2 rather than the notebook's fixed six; and BLME fixes the reference's Joseph accumulator bug. Each of those makes BLME's estimator lower-variance, not different in kind, and the measured agreement is <=3.2% on H and J.
paper_reason: Alabdulmohsin, Tran & Dehghani 2024 Table 1 gives, for the Pile's Wikipedia subdomain, S = 0.62 +/- 0.02, H = 0.74 +/- 0.01, J = 0.52 +/- 0.00. BLME on gpt2 over WikiText-103 validation (57 documents, 895 scored tokens each after a 128-token burn-in) gives J = 0.5118 (rel 1.6%, inside nothing but very close), S = 0.5626 (rel 9.3%) and H = 0.6002 (rel 18.9%). The H gap is a PROTOCOL gap, not an implementation gap: the released reference run on my identical streams gives H = 0.6045, i.e. it lands in the same place BLME does, and the paper's documents are >2K tokens (they filter to >2048 and score up to MAX_LENGTH) while gpt2's 1024-token context leaves BLME only 895 points -- R/S is biased low on short series. PARTIAL: J reproduces, S is close, H is systematically short and the reference reproduces the shortfall.
confounds_reason: Measured over 13 models (distilgpt2, gpt2, gpt2-medium, gpt2-large, pythia-70m/160m/410m/1b, opt-125m, SmolLM2-135M/360M, Qwen2.5-0.5B, Llama-3.2-1B) at the harness default eps: no |spearman| against d_model, n_layers or vocab_size reaches significance for any of the three pooled exponents (largest is joseph vs n_layers at +0.451, p ~ 0.12). The real instability is the FREE PARAMETER, not architecture -- see defects.
defects: THE CONFIG OVERRIDE WAS A REAL DEFECT AND ITS REMOVAL IS RIGHT, but the effect is WORSE than the ledger describes: at eps 5e-2 vs 5e-3 the pooled self_similarity_exponent does not merely shrink, it REORDERS models. Over the full validation split (57-58 documents) I measure gpt2 0.562563 -> 0.506790 (-9.9%), distilgpt2 0.428483 -> 0.282207 (-34.1%) and pythia-70m 0.573240 -> 0.750697 (+31.0%). A parameter that moves one model down 34% and another up 31% is not a scale factor.

At eps = 5e-3 the per-document estimate goes NEGATIVE, which is impossible for a Hoelder exponent (p_eps(tau) is non-increasing in tau, so S >= 0): distilgpt2 self_similarity_exponent_perdoc = -0.015737 at 57 documents and gpt2 = -0.134327 at 15. That is the estimator failing outright, exactly as the notebook's docstring warns, and it is a cleaner proof that 5e-3 is unusable than any percentage.

THE SOURCE COMMENT'S NUMBERS DO NOT REPRODUCE. The block above `_eps_ok` states, for gpt2, pooled 0.569557 -> 0.043773 (-92.3%), perdoc 0.667857 -> 0.470090 and std 0.668682 -> 0.057779. Two of the six quoted values match EXACTLY (perdoc and std at 5e-3), which pins the corpus, so the other four are from a different code state or a different column. CONFIG (the shipped study): dynamics_fractal: {num_samples: 100} against a WikiText prefix builds only THREE 4K-token documents on a solo run, because each document consumes ~30 corpus rows. I measure _meta_n_documents = 3 at pool 100, 15 at pool 500 and 57 at the full 1747-row split, and the pooled S moves 0.6704 / 0.5650 / 0.5626 across those three. The value therefore depends on the shared corpus size that other co-running tasks set -- the same coupling dynamics_interpolation was just fixed for, still live here. num_samples caps DOCUMENTS, not corpus rows, and nothing pins the pool.

The paper reports the MEDIAN fractal parameter over documents (Table 2 caption); BLME's headline is a single POOLED power-law fit and its secondary is a per-document MEAN. Neither is the paper's estimator, and the pooled/perdoc difference is not small (gpt2 S 0.5626 vs 0.5553 at 57 docs, but 0.6704 vs 0.5605 at 3 docs).

hurst_exponent_perdoc carries spearman -0.665 with d_model over 13 models while the pooled hurst_exponent carries -0.207. Both are feature-eligible and unprefixed, so the analysis can pick the depth-linked one.
